description:
Today I take a look at the GTX 1070 Gaming Z, which is the same as the Gaming X with the addition of an RGB light on the back.  Overall the card is really solid, has low noise, and performs really well out of the box.  
It also features the Samsung Memory for those of you that are worried.  I also take a solid look at the VRM which features UBIQ QM3616N6 Mosfets (relatively new).

You can get the GTX 1070 Gaming X here on sale at the moment - http://amzn.to/2f3UddG

If you want the exact one shown in this review (The Z) then you can get it here - http://amzn.to/2eGUcIW

Keep in mind Nvidia only officially support 2 way SLI in games with the release of Pascal (so buying a 3rd or even 4th card for gaming would just be problematic, so I don't recommend it)....

comments.text:
Samsung cards were manufactured up until the end of June 2016 and came with a bios version 86.04.1e.00.xx. From July up until sometime in September, all 1070 cards, including founders edition cards, were manufactured with Micron chips that came with a buggy bios 86.04.26.00.xx  that caused checkerboard artifacts and BSOD crashes without using a work around that only partially mitigated the problem that is only now being addressed with a bios update from Nvidia. The MSI one has not been released as of today although  EVGA, ASUS and Palit/Gainward have released their versions of the new 86.04.50.00.xx series of vbios. 

On top of that, MSI and Asus early on were caught out sending tweaked "reviewer" bioses that default to the OC mode instead of the default "gaming" mode to make the cards appear better out of the box than what they really were. The justification from MSI seemed to be saying that tech reviewers are too busy or too stupid to work out how to change the settings in the gaming app themselves when they are reviewing the card. 

The main issue for dissatisfaction over and above the fact that the Micron cards crashed and did weird things where the Samsung ones didn't and the frustration of spending $US400 on something that was flawed, has been:

1. There has been no Micron cards sent out to any professional English speaking tech review media on both youtube or web/print.
2. The few amateur/tiny review sites that looked at Micron cards either stated they didn't try to overclock the memory because the "memory was fast enough already" or ignored memory overclocking altogether rather than stating that they observed issues.
3. The "Reviewer" bios versions only exist for the bioses that came with the 86.04.1E.00.xx Samsung memory cards.
4. The Tech media's absolute silence on the issue. 

The first mention of anything to do with the micron issues was on the guru3d.com article last week that announced that the vendors were releasing a new bios update to address 1070 Micron issues. Very strange given that everyone is all over the EVGA heat problems and that only effects one vendor.

Please don't take this as a criticism of you personally, That is not my intention. It is very difficult  to comment on something that you are probably not aware of or have not had an opportunity to observe first hand due to teh apparent cherry picking of review samples sent to you.
